name: Z(π) copies through an H-box
summary: A Z-state with phase π on an H-box gives the |1⟩ state on all the other legs.
description:
Plugging the state $|0\rangle - |1\rangle$ (an arity-1 Z-spider with phase $\pi$) into a leg of an H-box with label $a$ gives $1 - a$ when all other legs are $1$, and $0$ otherwise. Hence the result is proportional to the basis state $|1\cdots 1\rangle$, i.e. an X-state with phase $\pi$ on every other leg. In terms of AND gates it says that post-selecting the output of an AND on $\langle 1|$ forces all its inputs to be $1$.

This is the only one of the basic derived rules of the phase-free ZH-calculus that needs the [ortho rule](../zh-ortho/). Conversely, together with [AND of a copied bit](../zh-dedup/) it can replace the ortho rule in the axiomatisation of the 2021 completeness paper.
parameter_notes: Shown for an H-box with n = 2 other legs; holds for any n.
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
